wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island on the eve of the midterm elections, a defeat JD Vance later blamed on the Iran war. Since then Trump has called new strikes highly unlikely, Mohsen Rezaei has denied any talks until seven conditions are met, and France says the Revolutionary Guards heated freezers in 700 French supermarkets.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The slide to a 10-week low came as further strikes on Iran looked unlikely, even as Iran claimed 11 tankers targeted in 10 days and one burned in Hormuz. Fire on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the route around the strait, did not reverse it, and China's October imports of nearly 42 million tons showed Gulf crude moving again.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The slide followed Trump calling a new Iran offensive "highly unlikely" if talks progress, which took Brent below $90 for the first time since August. Crude fell even as Iran's media said 11 tankers were targeted in 10 days around Hormuz and an attack set Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline ablaze.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The rebound from the late-October trough came as the Iran war made American gas a substitute for Gulf supply: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022, and QatarEnergy, whose exports pass through a disrupted Hormuz, agreed to buy up to 3 million tonnes of US liquefied natural gas a year.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The news that followed this reading ran on two tracks: Turkey offered Zelensky help restoring Ukraine's Black Sea grain corridor, and Punjab and Sindh reset Pakistan's own wheat support and release prices. Neither predates the latest figure, and neither accounts for its rise.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: AI demand pulled the metal up: Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton over London prices at Shanghai, and Mitsui Kinzoku is spending 190 billion yen on a Malaysia plant for the copper foil in AI server circuit boards. Then the same trade turned, and fears over AI sent copper to $13,778 a tonne, its lowest since July.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan then called for at least two more quarter-point hikes, possibly quickly. Waller and other Fed speakers turned hawkish too, and traders began pricing a half-point December hike instead of a quarter, which set off a global bond selloff.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fall was led by chipmakers after the midterms. A Democratic sweep, read as a backlash against data-centre building, sent Nvidia down 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% on Thursday, and the AI rout spread to Asia, where the Kospi fell 8%. The next day, US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against 65,000 forecast.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Anthropic's prospectus showed an $80.7 billion loss in six months, and after the midterms chip stocks broke: Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% in one session. Nvidia then lost another 6.27% as its board investigated Jensen Huang, briefly ceding second place in market value to Microsoft.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war's oil shock still sets the backdrop: Valero says freight to Asia now costs $30-$35 a barrel, a premium that favours US Gulf Coast refiners, and the US raised its forecasts for 2027 gasoline and diesel prices. Nothing in the fortnight's stories explains the easing at the pump itself.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The Iran war drove it: strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, and LNG shipping through Hormuz came under fire, with Qatar's carrier Al Mayeda later struck in the Gulf. European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour heading into winter, its highest since 2022.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's news carried tightening talk rather than a shock: the Fed's Waller said he would back at least a quarter-point rate hike in December, and US inflation dimmed risk appetite as Bitcoin slid. None of it falls on the day of the peak, so none of it explains the spike.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The Hormuz closure has made Pakistan's fuel-import bill, paid in dollars, more expensive. Gas rationing and nighttime power cuts already grip the country, and a tanker attack tested its Hormuz deal. Against that drain, UAE investors bought $395.7 million of Pakistan's bonds since July.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian business news was about where companies hold capital, not about the currency: Access Holdings reported 19.3% of its equity abroad, double the CBN's cap on foreign subsidiaries, and Dangote Cement shelved its London listing. Neither accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound's recovery from its late-October weakness tracked a rebound in one of Egypt's main dollar earners: the Suez Canal took $724 million in October, its highest monthly revenue since 2023 and up 94%, despite Houthi threats in the Red Sea.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news in these weeks was the Habaş steel plant blast in Aliağa, COP31 opening in Antalya and Erdoğan's rift with Aliyev. None of it was about monetary policy or the currency, and none of it explains the lira's steady slide.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: Garment factories, the country's largest source of dollars, were disrupted for three days as workers demanded 30,000 taka a month, up from 12,500, and Dhaka formed a wage board in response. Sheikh Hasina's application for a Bangladeshi passport was rejected. Nothing reported over the fortnight ties either event to the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Jakarta's fortnight was the wiretap scandal: the president's chief of staff was dismissed, three top police officers were arrested and 20,980 troops deployed. October inflation eased slightly to 3.23%. Nothing reported ties either to the rupiah's slide.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's reporting from Lebanon dealt with the cost of living, not the currency. Palestinian refugees in Beddawi, outside Tripoli, described being squeezed by high energy prices and inflation. None of it accounts for the rate's small drift.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Exporters in Ningbo are paying for the firmer yuan, which has gained 9% on the euro. Beijing is meanwhile widening its reach: 19 African countries can now settle in yuan without New York or London banks, and the digital yuan is going offshore through Hong Kong. None of that accounts for the day-to-day price.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI stepped in with likely dollar sales that lifted the rupee to 95.02, defending a currency that pays for India's imported oil in dollars. India's crude now arrives from about 43 countries, spreading the import bill that weighs on the rupee across more suppliers.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The slide began as Lula's election win came in and his defeated rival Flávio Bolsonaro flew to the US, with investors cooling on another Lula term. The central bank has since named the weaker real as one of four shocks pushing inflation past its target range, alongside oil from the Iran war, El Niño and the end of the 44-hour work week.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The Mexican news in this window was the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, who lost the fraud-marred 1988 election, and the arrest in Zapopan of a Jalisco cartel leader linked to Mayor Carlos Manzo's murder. Neither accounts for the peso's weakening.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022, as the Iran war's oil shock spread, and forecasters now see euro zone inflation averaging 3.0% this year, which has reopened talk of an ECB rate hike. Lagarde leaves on 7 February, and euro-area governments are choosing her successor, with Klaas Knot among the nominees.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Tokyo confirmed it spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, pushing back against a weakness that nearly half of Japan's manufacturers have already written into raised profit forecasts. The cheap currency also drew foreign borrowers, who sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds to fund AI spending.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The weeks led up to Abu Dhabi, where Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months under US brokerage, after Trump met Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House. Ukrainian drones also set the Kirishi refinery ablaze. None of the reporting ties any of it to the ruble's move.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The rand's strongest day came just after the US election results that Ramaphosa greeted as a new era. It came despite the US suspending South Africa from AGOA, under which it shipped $1.7 billion of duty-free exports in 2025. At home, local elections left 110 councils projected to hang as the ANC slid from 47.5% to 32.5%.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The slide followed the $6.3 billion Binance theft the FBI blames on North Korea's TraderTraitor, after which customers pulled a net $4.72 billion. The CLARITY Act then stalled 49 to 50 in the Senate, $1.26 billion in leveraged bets were liquidated as tech stocks fell, and spot ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion in a week.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The month's defining event was the theft of $6.3 billion from Binance, which the FBI blames on North Korea's TraderTraitor and North Korea denies. Binance covered 90% of the losses and resumed withdrawals, but selling spread across crypto, and Bitcoin dropped below $75,000 for the first time since September 15.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The rebound began with the US midterms: a Democratic sweep of Congress pushed the dollar and Treasury yields down, and December futures jumped 3% in a day. Chinese gold ETFs had already drawn $784 million in October buying the fall. A hot US inflation reading and Fed remarks then took back part of the gain.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators met in Abu Dhabi on 10 November under US brokerage, their first peace talks in 9 months, with the US seeking a new Europe security framework and Russia sending 5 senior officials. Around the table the war went on: Ukrainian drones set the Kirishi refinery ablaze, and Russian strikes cut power to about 850,000 people.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: US strikes on Qeshm Island ahead of the midterm elections came as an Iran commander set out five conditions for regional security, days after Tehran offered a 48-hour reopening plan. Since then mines on the Revolutionary Guards' route have set tankers ablaze, and Iraq and Pakistan have each struck their own deal for passage.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran's media say it targeted 11 tankers in 10 days, and two burned on a route it has banned. Exporters are routing around the strait: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was set ablaze, and Iraq is seeking a lane through Oman. Siam Cement's Vietnam plastics plant, cut off from Middle East naphtha, stays shut until mid-2027.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The Houthi war has turned inland on Saudi Arabia rather than onto ships: missiles at Riyadh, a strike on the East-West pipeline near Yanbu, debris through Aramco Tower, and Saudi strikes on Sanaa in return. Ships kept using the route, and Egypt's Suez Canal doubled its revenue to $724 million in October.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, its highest monthly revenue since 2023, as ships came back to the Red Sea route. The waters at its southern end stay contested: Egypt is moving off the sidelines in the Saudi-Houthi conflict, and Sudan's Burhan has offered Russia a Red Sea economic zone.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the far end of the oil route: tankers mined and set alight east of Hormuz, Iran's media claiming 11 tankers targeted in 10 days, and Valero putting freight to Asia at $30-$35 a barrel. None of it explains the traffic counted here.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The one strait story in the fortnight was Taipei's count of 53 Chinese ships around Taiwan, 34 of them warships. Nothing reported about them, or about any closure, accounts for the one-day collapse and rebound in traffic in late October.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Ships bound through the strait are sailing under fire: drones reportedly hit at least 7 in the Black Sea last month, sinking the Contship Jet off Bulgaria, and Russia struck 3 cargo ships near Odesa it said carried weapons to Ukraine. Zelensky says Turkey will help restore the grain corridor; the EU pledged €50 million for a Black Sea security hub.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's one shipping story was Treasury sanctioning a Chandigarh couple for faking Iranian tankers' flags. That is the shadow-fleet trade this strait is watched for, but nothing in the news explains the daily vessel count.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was about Hormuz, not the Cape: Iran's Guards said they set tankers ablaze and mined the strait, a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire, and Valero said freight to Asia now costs $30-$35 a barrel. None of it accounts for fewer ships rounding southern Africa.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Black Sea shipping came under fire elsewhere. Russia struck three cargo ships off Odesa that its defence ministry claimed carried weapons to Ukraine, and drones reportedly hit at least 7 Black Sea ships last month, prompting an EU security package. Nothing reported from the strait itself accounts for its empty traffic.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Türkiye's news this fortnight was the Habaş steel plant blast at Aliağa, COP31 opening in Antalya and Erdoğan's rift with Aliyev. None of it touches earnings, the lira or interest rates, and none of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's Malaysian news was political and corporate: Najib Razak left Kajang prison for house arrest after a $12.3M fine, Binance sought a licence to return, and Mitsui Kinzoku planned a $1.2bn copper foil plant. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia's political news was a wiretapping scandal: police detained three generals accused of tapping the president's phone, his chief of staff was dismissed, and 20,980 troops deployed in Jakarta. It broke after the slide had already bottomed, and nothing else reported from Indonesia accounts for the fall.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: AI worries hit Tokyo's tech stocks in late October, and the rout spread across Asia until South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. The rebound rode the weak yen: nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised profit forecasts, and Mitsubishi Corporation now forecasts record ¥1.2 trillion net income.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's news about Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies was mostly about their AI push: Tencent expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold, and Kuaishou's Kling unit raised about 19.8 billion yuan. The Pentagon also delisted WuXi AppTec after a court ruling. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The trough came at the end of October, when new export orders fell to 48.7 and third-quarter results showed the property sector losing 53.2 billion yuan even as tech profit rose 140%. Exporters were also squeezed by a yuan that had gained 9% on the euro, and the PBOC began setting a weaker fixing to slow its rise.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fall came as an AI rout spread from US markets to Asia. On Friday South Korea halted trading after the Kospi dropped 8% in one session, as selling hit the chipmakers whose AI-driven earnings carry the index, SK Hynix among them.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Jio Platforms listed 25% above issue price at $137.1 billion in India's largest initial public offering, leaving Ambani owning India's top two companies. Carmakers dispatched an estimated 525,000 cars to dealers in October, and likely RBI dollar sales lifted the rupee to 95.02 as oil prices pressed on it.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's own news in these weeks was a 500-tonne gold vault opened to foreign central banks, DayOne's filing for a Nasdaq listing and a US carrier's last port call before the Iran war. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: An AI rout spread to Asia in early November, and South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. A market this heavy in TSMC moves with chip stocks. The same week, about 12 Micron workers staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike, and Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight brought the US suspension of South Africa from AGOA, under which it exported $1.7 billion duty-free in 2025, and local elections that left 110 councils projected to hang as ActionSA took Gauteng townships from the ANC. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Flávio Bolsonaro's defeat kept Lula in office, and economists then raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34%. Brazil's central bank named four shocks behind the rise: oil from the Iran war, El Niño, the end of the 44-hour work week and a weaker real. Together they leave rates that already weigh on growth with no room to fall.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican news was political and criminal, not financial: the arrest in Zapopan of Rafael Alvarez, linked to the murder of Mayor Carlos Manzo, and the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at 92. A $573 million quarterly loss at Pemex, which is not a listed company, was the only corporate result, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada's business news this fortnight was about its break with the US: a paper mill in Témiscaming idled by tariffs, and a Montreal summit with the EU that dropped associate membership. Enbridge reported higher profit on natural gas and Barrick Mining filed to list its North American gold assets, but none of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Rates did the damage: core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, the Fed's Logan called for two more hikes, traders priced 78% odds of a December move, and two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points. Nvidia fell 6.27%, briefly ceding second place to Microsoft, as its board and House committees examined Jensen Huang.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The Bank of England raised rates on a forecast that inflation will peak at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on. Dangote Cement shelved its London listing as war-driven volatility drained appetite for emerging-market risk. Neither story is tied to the index's own path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight's German economic news was Nagel backing a third ECB rate hike this year in December, and Schaeffler cutting 3,500 jobs, three quarters of them in Germany. Neither accounts for the index's move.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's fortnight was one of domestic strain: Fitch cut its outlook after the economy shrank 0.1%, unions struck for wages, and Mélenchon promised nationalisations and a NATO exit. Lagarde also said she would leave the European Central Bank in February. None of that news is tied to the index's moves.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's news over these weeks was a rear-end train collision near Toledo that killed at least 68, a migrant emergency on El Hierro, and a two-way race between Knot and De Cos to replace Lagarde at the European Central Bank; none of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: What touched this market in the period was its banks: ECB policymakers brought a rate hike debate into the open, and the ECB urged Intesa to keep a cautious dividend policy after its MPS acquisition. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: Switzerland's news was about its currency, not its companies: the franc rose almost 1% as the US midterms weakened the dollar, Swiss inflation reached its highest in almost three years, and the SNB reported a nine-month profit on foreign currencies and gold. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The only Swedish story of the fortnight was the wave of cyberattacks that drove supermarket freezers to 50°C in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg. None of it touches the industrial and telecom companies that move this index.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The slide ran through a hung election, in which neither bloc reached 61 seats without Arab parties, and Trump's announcement ending $4 billion a year in US aid to Israel after 2026. The rebound came as 67 of 120 Knesset members recommended Eisenkot for prime minister, though he still needs the Arab parties' 19 seats from outside.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Democrats won Congress, flipping the Senate, and Vance called the Iran war 'the reason we lost'. Trump called the midterms dishonest, ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats and put Stephen Miller in place of Wiles as chief of staff, while saying strikes on Iran are highly unlikely after Gulf neighbours asked him to hold fire.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed held rates on 28 October despite intensifying inflation, and the next move traders now price is a hike. October brought 165,000 new jobs against 65,000 forecast and core prices up 0.3%; Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan called for two more hikes, and bonds sold off on the risk of a half-point step in December.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: Eurozone inflation hit 4% after eight straight months above 2%, pushed up by the Iran war's oil shock. The ECB held while Panetta and Nagel argued for a December hike. Lagarde leaves on 7 February, so the contest between Knot and De Cos is also a choice between hawk and dove for the rate path.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: October's report had US employers adding 165,000 jobs against 65,000 forecast, a labour market strong enough that Treasuries stumbled as traders raised their bets on another Fed hike. Fed's Barkin said the policy direction was clear but needed a careful pace.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's news on precious metals was about gold, which held near $4,000 through hot US inflation data and Fed remarks and gained after the US midterms, while China extended its gold-buying streak to two years. None of it explains silver's own slide.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged in October despite inflation, and the October price figure from BLS then slowed less than expected. That hot reading cemented bets on a December rate hike: Treasuries slid, Bitcoin dropped to almost a three-month low and gold held a loss near $4,000.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards let tankers through only on a route they control, and ships on the banned one have hit mines and burned: Iranian media count 11 tankers targeted in 10 days. Iraq secured its own export lane past Oman, while ADNOC Gas is studying new routes because LNG, unlike crude, has no Fujairah bypass.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The October return of container lines showed at the canal this strait feeds: Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million that month. Since then the Saudi–Houthi war has moved onto Saudi soil, with a Houthi refinery strike claim, an attack on the East-West pipeline near Yanbu and missile debris across Aramco Tower in Riyadh.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, revenue doubling as traffic climbed. Over the same weeks the Houthi war turned on Saudi Arabia itself, with strikes on Riyadh, on Aramco Tower and on the East-West pipeline near Yanbu, though nothing reported ties that shift to the canal's traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Much of the crude this strait carries to China first leaves through Hormuz. The IRGC halted two tankers there at the end of October, Iran then offered a 48-hour reopening plan, and China imported nearly 42 million tons of crude that month. Iraq has since secured an oil export lane through Hormuz.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: The fortnight's news from both shores was about French wage strikes, an Iranian Revolutionary Guards hack of supermarket freezers in France, and US aircraft leaving RAF Mildenhall. None of it touched shipping in the strait, and none of it explains the traffic.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news centred on Hormuz, where Iran's Guards set tankers alight on a route they had banned. None of it explains traffic at the Atlantic end of the Mediterranean.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia, Ukraine and the US opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi on 10 November. Washington is seeking a new security framework covering Europe, and a US official said Ukraine could get NATO-like guarantees. Two days earlier, Russian strikes left about 850,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk without power.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: US intelligence reportedly flagged Megaspeed's Alice Huang, who had an affair with Jensen Huang, as Beijing's asset; her employer reportedly bought $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment. The board opened a probe, House committees asked for a closed briefing 18 November, a Senate Banking Committee Republican urged him to resign, and Microsoft overtook Nvidia in market value.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple launched a touchscreen MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac, then reported a record quarter, with India carrying iPhone revenue. The same report forecast gross margin of 45-46%, down from 47.9%, as its new CEO called memory prices "unprecedented", and the shares shed about $140 billion after hours. In China, Alibaba's Qwen now powers Siri.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results showed capex up 114% to $51.4 billion in a single quarter, enough to turn its cash flow negative, alongside a miss in search. Since then Google has tied more of its balance sheet to Anthropic: it can take over Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease with TeraWulf, and it is buying $10 billion of Anthropic, as is Nvidia.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's results showed its 12-month cash burn at a record $42.4 billion, because spending on AI capacity ran ahead of what its retail and cloud businesses bring in. The report arrived the same week other big tech earnings disappointed, which deepened the sell-off.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: The slide ran into a sell-off in AI stocks that spread to Asia, where South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. A foundry whose most advanced output goes into the chips Nvidia designs sits at the centre of that trade.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft passed Nvidia in market value for the first time since June 2025, but on Nvidia's fall: its board is investigating Jensen Huang over ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence target. OpenAI, in which Microsoft holds a large stake, raised $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below the $1.4 trillion it first sought.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: The only news about Broadcom's own business in the fortnight was a product release: VMware's vSphere Express, for virtualization on up to 128 cores. Nothing in it accounts for the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX's default risk hit a fresh peak in a tech-led selloff, in the same week Musk's political bet failed. Through the window SpaceX weighed a merger with Tesla, which Barclays called a key part of the Tesla bull case, and a senior official has since described SpaceX as fundamentally an infrastructure company.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta spent the fortnight readying a cross-border investment-grade bond sale to pay for its AI build-out, and shelved business terms that claimed training rights over its customers' websites after objections in the EU and UK. Neither event accounts for the share's swings.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on oil prices lifted by the Hormuz crisis, and it began expanding the East-West pipeline that carries its crude around the strait. A day after debris from intercepted Houthi missiles blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, an unclaimed attack set that pipeline ablaze.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Musk is ending Cybertruck production to turn Tesla toward robotics and AI, after the pickup sold an estimated 11,586 units in nine months, by Cox Automotive's count. The shares jumped 4% the morning he killed it. Tesla now says its steering-wheel-free Cybercab meets federal safety standards, but has not explained how.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's quarterly results, released alongside Alphabet's, rattled technology shares. The same day it pulled fridges and washing machines from sale in Hong Kong, listing them as sold out. Days later it joined Tesla in opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: The steepest drop came in the chip selloff after the US midterms, when Micron lost 11% in a day alongside Nvidia and AMD. That same day, about 12 Micron workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike, and the company paused work on a planned Taiwan plant over the labour dispute.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD's third quarter beat estimates: data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion on AI chip demand, while its gaming business slumped. The gain did not last. Two days later a chip selloff after the midterms took 12% off AMD in one session, a steeper fall than Nvidia's.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one thing Walmart did in the news was join Eli Lilly and 36 other issuers in objecting to tokenized versions of their shares on OKX-ICE. That dispute is about where its stock trades, not about how its stores sell, and nothing in the input accounts for the price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: October came in at 4%, the eighth straight month above 2%, and forecasters now expect the year to average 3.0%, which has opened a debate at the ECB over raising rates. Nothing in these reports says what is driving prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The one Solana-specific development in the fortnight's news cut the other way: Schroders, a $1.1 trillion manager, chose the network to tokenize an emerging-market bond fund. Nothing in the input accounts for the token's fall.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: XRP fell with the rest of crypto. A Binance hack sent bitcoin and ether tumbling, a day after bitcoin's slide below $80,000 liquidated $356 million in crypto longs. An Nvidia-led tech selloff and mounting ETF outflows ahead of US inflation data then pushed bitcoin to an almost three-month low.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Hyperliquid drew attention for letting traders take 10-fold leveraged positions on Anthropic's initial public offering, a bet on a United States listing placed offshore, outside the venues that carry such contracts at home. Nothing in the input explains the token's slide since.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash climbed in two bursts that outran the rest of crypto: an 8% jump as Bitcoin neared $81,000 ahead of the Fed decision, then 12% more in the post-election rebound, with Bitcoin holding above $80,000. Nothing in the news since accounts for the fall that followed.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: This monthly reading predates the Bank of England's unanimous hike on 5 November, its first rise since 2023, which ended the run of cuts. The Bank now forecasts inflation peaking at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: BOJ chief Ueda said the 2% inflation goal was not yet sustainably achieved, then a week later saw "some upside risks" to it. Tokyo spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in a day buying yen, and Uniqlo reversed a sock price rise within days, the price resistance that keeps the BOJ cautious. Foreign yen bond sales hit a record $16 billion.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China's moves this fortnight were about the currency, not the cost of credit. It set a weaker yuan fixing and raised the forex deposit reserve requirement to slow a yuan rally fed by a record trade surplus, and none of that touched its lending rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia raised the path it projects for the key rate after putting fourth-quarter inflation at 7.1-7.6%. It said holding rates on that higher trajectory is what brings inflation down to 4% in 2027, which tempers the easing the bank had delivered.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The trough came the day Thai inflation hit 3.9%, above the central bank's ceiling. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has also reached Thai industry: Siam Cement's core plastics plant in Vietnam, cut off from Middle East naphtha, stays shut until mid-2027 while it switches to US ethane.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles reached the kingdom's commercial core: a strike on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on 10 October, debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower, and an attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze. Against that, Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion, and Qatar's PM called U.S. talks on Iran positive.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: On the day of the high, Trump signalled after a Qatar meeting that new Iran strikes were unnecessary, and Qatar's prime minister called the U.S. talks on Iran positive. That eased a war risk around the Strait of Hormuz: Brent had gained a fourth month on a U.S. threat to Iran, and Al Gharbia's pipeline output fell from 250,000 to 60,000 tonnes.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The economy under the index lost pace: growth slowed to 2.1% in Q3, dragged by inflation, and businesses were struggling to keep customers through a weak peso and high inflation. Philippine bonds were rated the most exposed in emerging Asia to Fed hikes.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta spent the period borrowing and retreating: it readied a cross-border investment-grade bond sale to pay for AI, and shelved business terms claiming training rights over its customers' websites after objections in Brussels. None of that, nor senators in Washington pressing it on glasses footage, explains the fall in the share.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The rise dates from Tencent's preview of Hunyuan Hy4, and within a week the company said it had expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold to keep up with WorkBuddy demand. The day before the preview, QuestMobile counted 143 million monthly users on Lvpaopao, its short-drama service.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Chip stocks fell on a data-centre backlash after the midterms, then US officials said Chinese intelligence had targeted Jensen Huang through Megaspeed's Alice Huang. Nvidia's board opened its own probe, House committees asked him for a closed briefing on 18 November, shareholders sued, and Microsoft briefly passed Nvidia in market value.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators opened US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, where Washington is seeking a 'final end' to the war and a US official floated NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Xi and China have no seat at those talks, so they bear on a Trump–Putin settlement, not on the three-way meeting this contract needs.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: The slide began with the quarter's results: search revenue missed, capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion and free cash flow turned negative, and Google conceded that AI search makes less money. It has kept committing since, buying $10 billion of Anthropic and backstopping Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease with TeraWulf.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The fortnight brought escalation, not talks: Houthis claimed strikes inside the kingdom, intercepted missiles blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and Houthis said Saudi-led strikes killed 27 villagers. Riyadh signed a defense pact with Damascus. None of it points to a truce.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: No negotiation stood behind the contract. Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran is not talking to Washington and that the US must first meet seven conditions from the June interim agreement. Trump held off strikes at the request of Gulf neighbours, and Rubio's talks stalled. Nothing in the fortnight put Iran's uranium on a table.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia, Ukraine and the US opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, but Washington arrived seeking a new security framework covering Europe that the EU had already rebuffed, and Russian strikes left 850,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk without power two days earlier. The only ceasefire agreed was local: Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Abu Dhabi brought Russia, Ukraine and the US to the table on 10 November, their first peace talks in 9 months. Trump met Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House beforehand, Russia sent 5 senior officials, and a US official floated NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Brussels rejected Trump's push for a deal covering all of Europe.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple reported a record quarter carried by India, where iPhone revenue defied price pressures, but its new CEO called memory chip prices "unprecedented" and guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%. About $140 billion of value went in after-hours trading, and Apple raised prices.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's top security official, said there are no negotiations with Washington and that the US must first meet seven conditions from the June interim agreement, which have gone unanswered. That cut against the Qatari mediation track, and Abbas Araghchi promised hell if US strikes resume, even as Trump held fire.

stocks:INTC.standing: The American chipmaker that both designs processors and makes them in its own fabs, the largest US bid at leading-edge manufacturing. Its share price answers to Washington's industrial policy as much as to PC and server demand.
stocks:INTC.recent: Intel beat its own revenue guidance and still lost 23% after hours as its PC chip sales plunged, while fears over AI spending hit tech earnings. The fall knocked $12B off the US government's stake. Days later in Shanghai it pitched Xeon chips to China's AI buyers, saying one supports over 1,000 AI agents.

stocks:BIDU.standing: Baidu runs China's dominant search engine and has staked its next chapter on artificial intelligence: its Ernie models, its cloud business and its Apollo Go robotaxis. Its US-listed shares trade on Nasdaq.
stocks:BIDU.recent: The fortnight brought Baidu product news, not results: in Shenzhen its Apollo unit showed Apollo World, a model that generates traffic reacting to the car so robotaxis can train on simulated scenarios, and in Wuhan its AI agent began turning residents' group chats into work orders. Neither accounts for the slide in the share.

stocks:BABA.standing: The New York-listed shares of China's largest e-commerce group, owner of Taobao and Tmall and the country's biggest cloud provider. The price carries Chinese consumer demand, Beijing's regulation and US-China tension.
stocks:BABA.recent: Apple chose Alibaba's Qwen to run its iPhone AI in China, Siri included, putting the group's model on Chinese iPhones. Around Singles Day, Alibaba also sold nearly 100,000 monthly AI passes at one fen each to pull users onto its models. Nothing in the reporting explains the slide that came before the Apple deal.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs one of China's largest short-video and livestreaming apps, the main rival to ByteDance's Douyin, and owns the Kling AI video generator. Advertising, livestream tips and e-commerce pay for it.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kling, Kuaishou's AI video unit, closed a record funding round of about 19.8 billion yuan, and the raise valued it above its parent, so a subsidiary is now priced at more than the platform that owns it. The round closed just after the late-October trough, and the shares recovered from there.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: Thousands joined the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' march in New Delhi demanding the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll bias, and Ashok Gehlot alleged dissent suppression ahead of it. Nothing reported in those days showed a move to remove Gyanesh Kumar, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-will-helen-zille-be-the-next-mayor-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Helen Zille, the former Cape Town mayor and Western Cape premier, becomes Johannesburg's next mayor. The city council elects the mayor, so coalition deals can matter as much as the vote.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: Washington stepped back from renewed strikes: Trump called them highly unlikely and said Gulf neighbours had asked him to hold fire while Qatar mediated. Tehran kept up the pressure in words instead. Abbas Araghchi promised hell if strikes resume, and Mohsen Rezaei said there are no talks until the US meets seven conditions.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on bitcoin each day. Bitcoin is a digital currency with a capped supply and no central issuer, so price shocks, hacks and rule changes send newcomers to look it up.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: None of the fortnight's news explains the mid-October peak. What it did carry: Chainalysis confirmed at least $5.9 billion stolen from Binance in a hack linked to North Korea, the CLARITY Act stalled 49 to 50 in the Senate after a Democratic sweep, and spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion in a week.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump said strikes on Iran were highly unlikely and that Gulf neighbours had asked him to hold fire. That came after Vance blamed the Iran war for the midterm election defeat, and as the House began voting to advance the impeachment of Hegseth. Rezaei denied any talks with Washington, so the cooling rests on US politics rather than a deal.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator from Georgia, becomes his party's presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Trump says strikes on Iran are highly unlikely after Gulf neighbours asked him to hold fire, but holding fire is not a deal to lift the blockade. Mohsen Rezaei says there are no talks with Washington until it meets seven conditions from the June interim agreement, and Iran targeted 11 tankers in 10 days.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: The price eased as Israel's election turned against Netanyahu: 67 of 120 Knesset members recommended Eisenkot for prime minister, and Trump announced an end to $4 billion in annual US aid to Israel after 2026. Netanyahu still holds caretaker power over Gaza, where Israel has kept the Rafah crossing shut.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said there were no talks with Washington, and that the US must first meet seven conditions from the June interim agreement. That cut against the Qatari mediation track. Trump said Gulf neighbours had asked him to hold fire, while Tehran said 2 tankers burned on its banned Hormuz route.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: October consumer prices rose more than expected, with core up 0.3%, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan answered by calling for at least two more quarter-point hikes, possibly quickly. Waller and other Fed speakers turned hawkish too, and two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points as bonds sold off.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares of the US electric-car and battery maker led by Elon Musk. Its valuation rests far more on promised robotaxis and robots than on the cars it sells today, so the stock often moves on Musk's plans as much as on its results.
stocks:TSLA.recent: Musk's political bet failed at the midterms, raising questions over Tesla's China ties, and Tesla opposed new US tariffs on Vietnam. Then it said it would wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas next year after weak sales and recalls, with 11,586 sold in nine months by Cox Automotive's estimate, as Musk turns to robotics and AI.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on the waterway that carries Gulf oil and gas to the world.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said there are no talks with Washington until the US meets seven conditions from the June interim agreement, undercutting the Qatari mediation track. Trump held off strikes at Gulf neighbours' request, and Iran said two tankers burned on a Hormuz route it bans.
